angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,004,591 km at 121.60 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.2238 +/- 0.0327 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 121.60 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.444 +/- 0.034 solar radii from Chakrabarty & Sengupta 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-33 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158...39C/abstract): 1,004,591 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.495 +/- 0.031 solar masses from Chakrabarty & Sengupta 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-33 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158...39C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 7430 +/- 100 K from Chakrabarty & Sengupta 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-33 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158...39C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Chakrabarty & Sengupta 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-33 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158...39C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-33.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.294, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-33 (pscomppars): spectral type A, from Watanabe et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.512.4404W/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-33 (pscomppars): [M/H] 0.1 dex, from Zhang et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155...83Z/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-33 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.81944, from Johnson et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...810L..23J/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 328636019723252096, flags_flame 00: age_flame 0.86461663 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 0.58951247 to 1.1395178)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-33 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 85.6 km/s, from Watanabe et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.512.4404W/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
